extracted.intended_audience: General readers, researchers, journalists, activists, and others seeking information about the National Coalition Against Censorship and free-expression advocacy
extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia article summarizing the National Coalition Against Censorship (NCAC): its mission, focus areas, programs, history, membership, and activities in defending freedom of expression. Useful for readers wanting an overview of the group's goals and resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assist those opposing censorship in schools and libraries
rubrics_metrics.description: Assist students, teachers, librarians, parents and others opposing censorship in schools and libraries
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of NCAC's stated mission; implies offering strategies, resources, and direct assistance to individuals and institutions facing censorship in educational settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work with artists and cultural institutions resisting art censorship
rubrics_metrics.description: Work with artists, curators and museum directors resisting art censorship
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit mission item; implemented through programs such as the Arts & Culture Advocacy Program (ACAP) to support art-world actors confronting censorship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inform public officials, media, and public about First Amendment rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Inform public officials, the media, and the general public about First Amendment rights and obligations
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NCAC positions itself as an educational and informational resource to improve understanding of free-speech law and obligations among officials, journalists, and the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advocate for public policies and laws respecting First Amendment principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Advocate for public policies and laws that respect First Amendment rights and principles
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy advocacy is a core activity — NCAC seeks legal and legislative outcomes aligned with First Amendment protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Educate young people about the First Amendment and free expression
rubrics_metrics.description: Educate young people about the First Amendment and the importance of free expression
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Youth-targeted outreach (e.g., Youth Free Expression Program) to raise awareness and build support for free-expression norms among younger audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage and support a nationwide activist network and local activism
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage with a nationwide network of activists and support local activism
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NCAC works through coalition members and grassroots actors to amplify local efforts and foster coordinated responses to censorship incidents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify, analyze censorship trends and develop strategies to promote free speech
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and analyze censorship trends and develop new strategies to promote free speech rights
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizational research and strategy development to detect patterns in censorship and craft effective responses and interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope: defend free expression across all media and specialized programs
rubrics_metrics.description: NCAC is concerned with censorship across all media including art, literature, and film; it works on several fronts through its programs (Arts & Culture Advocacy Program, Youth Free Expression Program, Kids' Right to Read Project)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates broad topical scope and program-based approach; suggests NCAC evaluates and acts on censorship issues across multiple media and audience contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain and publish a crowdsourced database of censorship incidents (Censorpedia)
rubrics_metrics.description: NCAC's online resources include CENSORPEDIA, a crowdsourced wiki for censorship incidents
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A documented resource for tracking and publicizing censorship incidents; implies a standard of transparency and community contribution to incident reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide guidance (Artists Rights) on what art is protected by the First Amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: Artists Rights, a guide intended for artists and arts professionals containing explanations of art that is (and is not) protected by the First Amendment of the U.S. Constitution
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical guidance resource explaining legal protections and limits for artistic expression; used to advise artists and institutions when assessing censorship risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assist with strategies/resources for resisting censorship and publicizing cases
rubrics_metrics.description: NCAC assists individuals, community groups, and institutions with strategies and resources for resisting censorship and creating a climate hospitable to free expression; it also encourages the publicizing of cases of censorship and has a place to report instances of censorship on the organization's website
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combines direct assistance (legal/advocacy/educational) with mechanisms for reporting and publicizing incidents — guidance for when and how to elevate particular cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal standard for obscenity (Miller v. California)
rubrics_metrics.description: The First Amendment does not protect obscene speech and defined obscene as something lacking serious literary, artistic, or scientific value (per Miller v. California)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited legal test/standard that limits First Amendment protection; relevant when NCAC evaluates whether contested material is constitutionally protected. This is the court-defined criterion referenced as motivating NCAC's formation.
